source_note: Real-world job postings. Plain-text transcriptions provided by the project owner (evaluation/m10/source/*.txt) -- NOT claimed byte-exact to the original postings; see docs/evaluation/MILESTONE_10A_REALWORLD_PARSING_FAILURES.md Section 0/F for exactly what fidelity is and is not guaranteed (valid UTF-8, no BOM, real Unicode punctuation preserved -- but not verified against the original listing itself). Unlike evaluation/m9b/corpus.json (individually-authored sentences wrapped into a synthetic posting), each entry here preserves the FULL, REAL, multi-section document structure -- this milestone's own finding is specifically about cross-section/heading behavior that a single-sentence-at-a-time corpus structurally cannot surface. CORRECTION (post-first-draft): this file's labels (is_requirement, category_annotation, ideal_outcome, acceptable_fallback) were FORMALIZED INTO THIS FILE AFTER diagnostic parser runs against both real postings had already been observed in the same working session -- NOT before, unlike M9B's own corpus. They are RETROSPECTIVE evaluation judgments, not a blind pre-registration; do not cite this file as evidence of pre-parser independence. See tests/test_m10a_evaluation_integrity.py's own module docstring and MILESTONE_10A_REALWORLD_PARSING_FAILURES.md Section 0/D for the full, honest account.

sections.notes: Culture/mission narrative plus a 'what you might learn' technology-exposure paragraph. Not in any heading table (_REQUIRED_HEADINGS/_PREFERRED_HEADINGS/_RESPONSIBILITY_HEADINGS/_SKIP_HEADINGS).
No heading category for 'things the candidate will learn/be exposed to' exists at all today -- distinct from both REQUIRED and RESPONSIBILITY.

Semantically a required-qualifications section. NOT an exact match for any _REQUIRED_HEADINGS entry ("requirements"/"required qualifications"/"qualifications"/"minimum qualifications"/"basic qualifications"/"must have(s)") -- "required skills" uses a different noun.
Company history/bio. Not an exact match for _SKIP_HEADINGS's "about us"/"about the company" (company-name-specific heading).

claims.text: The technologies you learn during an internship at SOTI range from learning to develop middle tier services using languages like C#, or deepening your knowledge of databases by leveraging SQL and learning how to build high performance apps using storage procedures.

ideal_outcome.rationale: Explicitly frames C#/SQL as POSSIBLE learning exposure during the internship ("the technologies you learn... range from..."), never a candidate qualification. Must produce zero JobRequirement rows.

claims.notes: CONFIRMED LIVE FALSE POSITIVE: current parser produces a REQUIRED alternative_concept_ids=('language.csharp','language.sql') row from this exact sentence.

claims.text: Enhance your programming skills by working in a team alongside experienced team members

ideal_outcome.rationale: Describes a learning activity the intern will do, not a qualification the candidate must already have.

acceptable_fallback.rationale: If a trace is produced at all despite this being a non-requirement, a bare diagnostic (never a scored row) is the only tolerable outcome.

claims.notes: CONFIRMED LIVE: currently an unparsed_claim (tolerable, not ideal -- ideally this section is never claim-gated as a requirement source at all).

claims.text: Gain an understanding of how various roles work together to deliver software products: Developers, Architects, Quality Assurance, User Experience, Product Management, Software Development, Marketing, etc.

claims.notes: CONFIRMED LIVE: currently an unparsed_claim.

ideal_outcome.rationale: Learning-outcome narrative, not a requirement. Also note: the word 'requirements' here refers to USER requirements gathering as a process the intern will learn about -- not a job requirement.

claims.notes: CONFIRMED LIVE, HIGHER SEVERITY: this sentence never even becomes a segmentation Claim at all (zero trace anywhere -- not requirements, not unparsed_claims). Worse than the acceptable_fallback, though the underlying semantic judgment (no requirement) happens to be satisfied by accident, not by design.

claims.text: Understand the tools and processes used to develop professional software products e.g. Jira, Git

ideal_outcome.rationale: Learning-outcome narrative naming example tools the intern will be exposed to, not a requirement that the candidate already know Jira/Git.

claims.notes: CONFIRMED LIVE, HIGHER SEVERITY: never becomes a Claim at all -- zero trace anywhere, same as m10a-soti-04.

claims.text: Understand the testing processes and frameworks used to deliver high quality software products
claims.notes: CONFIRMED LIVE, HIGHER SEVERITY: never becomes a Claim at all -- zero trace anywhere.

claims.text: Required skills:

ideal_outcome.rationale: This is a SECTION HEADING, not a requirement sentence at all. A correctly-recognized heading never becomes its own Claim.

claims.notes: CONFIRMED LIVE FALSE POSITIVE: because "required skills" is not in _REQUIRED_HEADINGS, this heading line itself is treated as ordinary body text (triggers the bare 'skills?' keyword in _REQUIREMENT_SIGNAL) and becomes its own spurious Claim, landing in unparsed_claims.

claims.text: Knowledge of algorithms, data structures and database fundamentals

ideal_outcome.rationale: Genuine technical competency, no single named product -- the maximally-correct, non-fabricating outcome is the existing conservative placeholder shape, never a fabricated concept.

acceptable_fallback.rationale: Tolerable (not ideal) given this is the SAME root-cause category (gerund/noun-phrase competency with no named product) M9F already evaluated and explicitly deferred.

claims.notes: CONFIRMED LIVE: currently an unparsed_claim (acceptable_fallback met, ideal_outcome not met). Matches M9F's category-3 taxonomy exactly.

claims.text: Basic knowledge of Software Development Life Cycle concepts
claims.notes: CONFIRMED LIVE: currently an unparsed_claim. Additional structural note: _TECHNICAL_LEAD_IN never even gets a chance here -- the claim starts with 'Basic knowledge of', not the exact anchored 'knowledge of' the regex requires.

claims.text: Strong math, analytic and problem-solving skills
claims.notes: CONFIRMED LIVE: currently an unparsed_claim.

claims.text: Basic knowledge of programming in one or more of the following programming languages: C, C++, Java, JavaScript, SQL, Ruby, Rust, Lua, Haskell

ideal_outcome.rationale: A genuine ANY-of-9 technology enumeration. The maximally-correct outcome preserves ANY-of semantics across every real, named technology -- fabricating zero extra options (no 'unresolved:one'/'unresolved:more' artifacts from the idiomatic 'one or more').

acceptable_fallback.rationale: The existing conservative 'unsafe' fallback is tolerable (preserves a trace, fabricates nothing) but loses the ANY-of-9 structure entirely.

claims.notes: CONFIRMED LIVE: currently resolves to the 'unsafe' conservative placeholder (category='alternative_requirement', concept_id=None) -- acceptable_fallback met, zero fabrication (unlike an illustrative reconstruction tried earlier in this investigation, which DID fabricate an 'unresolved:one' option for a differently-punctuated version of this idiom -- see MILESTONE_10A doc Section 3 for why the exact phrasing determines which of the two failure modes fires). ideal_outcome (full 9-language alternative group) is NOT met.

claims.text: Most importantly curiosity, a desire to learn and be a part of a team

ideal_outcome.rationale: A genuine, if vague, soft-skill/personality-trait requirement -- GitHub evidence cannot speak to curiosity or desire-to-learn at all. The maximally correct outcome is the existing soft_skill non-technical placeholder, matching how 'teamwork'/'communication skills' are already handled elsewhere in this exact posting (m10a-man-12).

acceptable_fallback.rationale: A bare diagnostic trace is tolerable if the non-technical pattern table does not happen to cover this exact phrasing.

claims.notes: CONFIRMED LIVE, HIGHEST SEVERITY: never becomes a segmentation Claim at all -- zero trace anywhere, not even unparsed_claims. Root cause: contains none of segmentation's outside-heading _REQUIREMENT_SIGNAL trigger words ('curiosity'/'desire'/'team' are not in that list; 'team' alone is not a trigger either), and 'Required skills:' (the heading immediately above it) was never recognized, so this bullet is judged by the same loose, accidental gate as ordinary prose.

sections.notes: Not an exact match for _RESPONSIBILITY_HEADINGS ("responsibilities"/"what you'll do"/"what you will do"/"the role"/"duties"/"key responsibilities") -- "Position Responsibilities" has an extra leading word.

Exact match for _PREFERRED_HEADINGS. Correctly recognized -- but see Section field 'necessity_hint_sticky_from_here' below: because every heading AFTER this one fails to match, every claim for the REST OF THE DOCUMENT inherits this section's PREFERRED necessity_hint.
Benefits-adjacent narrative. Not in any heading table.
Pay-transparency disclosure paragraph, no heading of its own.
Company-name-specific heading; not an exact match for _SKIP_HEADINGS's generic 'about us'/'about the company'.
Equal-opportunity/accommodation legal text, no heading of its own in this posting.
Final line, posting is truncated at this heading in the provided transcription -- category genuinely unknown without the text that would have followed it.

necessity_hint_sticky_from_here.starting_claim: Exposure to software frameworks, libraries, or development tools
necessity_hint_sticky_from_here.rationale: CONFIRMED LIVE: every single claim from here through the end of the 54-line posting -- spanning 'When you join our team', 'Application instructions', the salary disclosure, 'About Manulife and John Hancock', the entire EEO/accommodation paragraph, and 'Working Arrangement' -- carries necessity_hint=PREFERRED, because current_kind is never reset once a heading fails to match, and it was last successfully set by 'Preferred Qualifications:'. This is Root Cause 2 in docs/evaluation/MILESTONE_10A_REALWORLD_PARSING_FAILURES.md, and it is the single most consequential finding of this corpus.

claims.text: As a Software Engineering Co-op, you’ll gain hands-on experience developing applications and systems that support business and customer solutions.

acceptable_fallback.rationale: A heading becoming a diagnostic-only claim (not a scored requirement) is tolerable, unlike SOTI's 'Required skills:' which is read-only text here too, consistent.

claims.notes: CONFIRMED LIVE: currently an unparsed_claim (acceptable, not ideal).

ideal_outcome.rationale: A duty/responsibility statement, not a candidate qualification to assess evidence against. GitHub evidence has nothing to verify here regardless.

claims.notes: CONFIRMED LIVE, HIGHEST SEVERITY: never becomes a segmentation Claim at all -- zero trace anywhere. Does not even meet the acceptable_fallback.

claims.notes: CONFIRMED LIVE, HIGHEST SEVERITY: never becomes a Claim -- zero trace anywhere.

claims.notes: CONFIRMED LIVE, HIGHEST SEVERITY: never becomes a Claim -- zero trace anywhere, despite containing 'collaborat*', which IS a recognized soft_skill keyword inside non_technical.py's own pattern table -- but that table is only ever consulted AFTER a Claim already exists; segmentation's own, different, narrower outside-heading gate (_REQUIREMENT_SIGNAL) does not include 'collaborat*' at all, so this sentence never reaches that stage.

claims.text: Participate in code reviews and maintain code quality standards
claims.notes: CONFIRMED LIVE, HIGHEST SEVERITY: never becomes a Claim -- zero trace anywhere.

claims.notes: CONFIRMED LIVE, HIGHEST SEVERITY: never becomes a Claim -- zero trace anywhere. All SIX 'Position Responsibilities' bullets (m10a-man-03 through 08) are completely, silently erased -- a full section, 100% invisible, not even partially mitigated by the existing unparsed_claims diagnostic.

claims.text: Currently pursuing an undergraduate degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field

ideal_outcome.rationale: A genuine education requirement, correctly NOT_OBSERVABLE -- GitHub evidence cannot speak to enrollment status at all.

claims.notes: CONFIRMED LIVE: already correct today -- category='education', necessity=required, NOT_OBSERVABLE. No defect here.

claims.text: Experience with at least one programming language (e.g., Java, Python, Go, JavaScript)

ideal_outcome.rationale: An ANY-ONE-of-4 requirement -- 'at least one of' is explicit OR semantics. The maximally correct outcome is a SINGLE alternative-group row, satisfied if the candidate shows evidence for ANY ONE of the four.

acceptable_fallback.rationale: A conservative, non-fabricating placeholder that preserves necessity and a trace, even if it loses the ANY-of structure, is tolerable. FOUR INDEPENDENT REQUIRED ROWS IS NOT AN ACCEPTABLE FALLBACK -- it materially changes assessment semantics (see notes).

claims.notes: CONFIRMED LIVE, MATERIAL FAIRNESS DEFECT (distinct failure mode from the SOTI 'one or more of' case -- this phrasing contains NO literal 'or' at all, using '(e.g., ...)' instead, so classify_alternative_claim's contains_alternative_marker() check never even fires). Produces FOUR SEPARATE, INDEPENDENTLY-ASSESSED required rows (language.java, language.python, language.javascript, unresolved:go) under the existing 'one row per matched concept per claim' design -- meaning a candidate who knows only Python would show 1 of 4 REQUIRED rows supported, not the correct '1 of 1 any-of-group satisfied.' This DIRECTLY SHRINKS the required subscore for a candidate who legitimately meets this requirement -- a false-negative fairness defect, the opposite direction from every other finding in this corpus (which inflate scores or lose traces, never unfairly penalize a qualified candidate).

claims.text: Familiarity with version control systems (e.g., Git, Bitbucket)

ideal_outcome.rationale: Genuine named-tool requirement (Git, Bitbucket), neither currently registered in the concept registry. A maximally correct outcome preserves both as unresolved:<term> placeholders, or at minimum ONE conservative placeholder, never zero rows.

claims.notes: CONFIRMED LIVE: currently an unparsed_claim (acceptable, not ideal). Note: 'version control systems' is itself a real, GitHub-observable-in-principle competency (a candidate's own commit history IS version-control evidence) with no named product required at all to assess it in principle -- flagged as a second-order design question, not a defect of this specific parser path.

claims.text: Strong communication skills and willingness to learn in a collaborative environment
claims.notes: CONFIRMED LIVE: already correct today -- category='soft_skill', necessity=required, NOT_OBSERVABLE. No defect.

claims.text: Exposure to software frameworks, libraries, or development tools

ideal_outcome.rationale: Vague, no named product -- correct necessity here IS preferred, since the heading correctly set it (unlike every later claim in this posting).

claims.notes: CONFIRMED LIVE: already correct -- category='unresolved_requirement', necessity=preferred (correctly derived from the properly-recognized 'Preferred Qualifications:' heading, not yet affected by the sticky-hint defect, which only starts affecting claims AFTER this section).

claims.text: Understanding of software development lifecycle and best practices
claims.notes: CONFIRMED LIVE: currently an unparsed_claim (acceptable, not ideal) -- 'Understanding of' is not one of the six recognized technical lead-in phrases, same gap as SOTI's 'Strong understanding of'.

claims.text: Familiarity with APIs, web services, or application architecture

ideal_outcome.rationale: Vague, no single named product; 'or' here is NOT a real technology enumeration (APIs/web services/application architecture are generic nouns, not named products) -- the maximally correct outcome is still the existing conservative non-fabricating placeholder, never a structured alternative group of fake 'technologies'.

claims.notes: CONFIRMED LIVE: already correct -- category='unresolved_requirement', necessity=preferred. The bare 'or' correctly does NOT get treated as a real alternative group here, because none of the three OR-segments resolves to (or shape-passes as) a real named technology -- classify_alternative_claim correctly falls through to not_technical. This is a useful POSITIVE control: 'or' alone is not always harmful.

claims.notes: CONFIRMED LIVE FALSE POSITIVE: produces a PREFERRED, category='unresolved_requirement' row -- a pay-transparency disclosure sentence rendered as a scored, necessity-bearing candidate requirement. Root cause: comma + 'such as' enumeration cue triggers _unresolved_requirement_signal's second check, and the STICKY preferred hint (this posting's Root Cause 2) supplies the necessity with no local override.

claims.text: This posting supports an ongoing hiring initiative for existing and/or future vacancies.

ideal_outcome.rationale: A statement about the POSTING/REQ itself, not about the candidate at all.

claims.notes: CONFIRMED LIVE FALSE POSITIVE: produces a PREFERRED, category='unresolved_requirement' row. Root cause: 'and/or' contains a word-boundary-matched literal 'or' (surrounded by '/' and a space, both non-alphanumeric), firing contains_alternative_marker() purely on an idiomatic administrative phrase with zero technical content, plus the sticky preferred hint.

claims.notes: CONFIRMED LIVE FALSE POSITIVE: produces a PREFERRED, category='unresolved_requirement' row purely from the comma+'such as' enumeration-cue shape, with zero semantic connection to any candidate skill, plus the sticky preferred hint.

claims.text: About Manulife and John Hancock
claims.notes: CONFIRMED LIVE: unparsed_claim.

claims.text: Manulife Financial Corporation is a leading international financial services provider, helping people make their decisions easier and lives better.
claims.notes: CONFIRMED LIVE: unparsed_claim (acceptable).

claims.text: To learn more about us, visit https://www.manulife.com/en/about/our-story.html.

ideal_outcome.rationale: A sentence pointing to a URL for more company information. Contains no technical requirement of any kind.

claims.notes: CONFIRMED LIVE, MOST CONCRETE FALSE POSITIVE IN THIS CORPUS: produces a PREFERRED, concept_id='language.html' row. Root cause: concepts.matching.alias_pattern()'s word-boundary regex (?<![A-Za-z0-9])html(?![A-Za-z0-9]) treats the '.html' file extension in the URL as a standalone token, because the characters surrounding it ('.' before, '.' after, both from the URL/sentence punctuation) are non-alphanumeric -- identical to how it would treat the English word 'html' in prose. A job posting literally has its own company-bio URL misread as 'requires HTML language experience.'
